source_documents.title: H ‐Aggregated Cationic Isomers to Boost ROS Generation for Photodynamic Therapy

reference_evidence_units.quote: the formation of H-aggregates at high concentrations actually enables effective generation of the photodynamic effect
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-IVQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: 2-IVQ forms H-aggregates more readily; ROS generation rises at high concentration.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: ROS assays; no triplet measured directly.

reference_evidence_units.quote: at low concentrations, 2-IVQ exhibits a weaker photodynamic effect compared to 4-IVQ, which further supports the formation of H-aggregates in 2-IVQ at high concentrations
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-IVQ vs 4-IVQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Concentration dependence of ROS generation compared with the isomer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Haggregated fluorophores would reach a special singlet excitation state with forbidden irradiation transition pathway to ground state, thus increasing the ISC efficiency to form triplet states for ROS generation
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-IVQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Dark lower exciton state of the H-aggregate lengthens the singlet lifetime and favours ISC.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: H-aggregation (Kasha exciton coupling, dark lower state) is the design principle and main explanation.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Enhanced ISC in the H-aggregate is proposed to explain ROS generation; no triplet measurement.
